summary:
# NOTES: THE DUKE DECIDES (Headon Hill; 21 chapters + closing section)

## Cast
- **Charles Hanbury / 7th Duke of Beaumanoir** (the Duke): ex-cavalry subaltern, lame (hatchway fall on voyage), poor; NY dry-goods clerk, $8/wk ($5 to boarding-house). Full name Charles Augustus Trevor Fitzroy Hanbury. Rent-roll £200,000/yr. Seat: Prior's Tarrant, Herts. Town house: Beaumanoir House, Piccadilly.
- **Jevons**: stout, fair Cockney, Panama hat; recruits Hanbury in Bowery saloon.
- **Clinton Ziegler**: alias of Cora Lestrade. White beard, purple puffy cheeks, blue/green glasses, invalid chair, piping/parrot voice. Hotel Cecil, first-floor suite.
- **Marker**: spy, covert-coat, tweed cap, cigar in holder; St. Paul cabin neighbour; later Elstree/Radlett train intruder.
- **Leonie Sherman**: American, dainty, Senator's daughter. **Mrs. Sherman** (Senator's wife, simple, admires aristocracy). **Senator Leonidas Sherman** (Washington; ex-Visiting Prison Commissioner; carries £3m US Treasury bonds).
- **Alec Forsyth**: Duke's Eton friend, Scot, Foreign Office 3rd-grade clerk, £230/yr; later secretary; loves Sybil. Lodges John Street, Adelphi.
- **General Jem Sadgrove**: 60, iron-grey, C.B., ex-Indian Staff (Thuggee/Dacoity); 140 Grosvenor Gardens. **Mrs. Madge Sadgrove**.
- **Azimoolah Khan**: Pathan, General's ex-orderly, valet; tracker, disguised as "Thakore of Bhurtnagur."
- **Sybil Hanbury**: 18, cousin, orphan, hoyden, in mourning; ruled Beaumanoir House; fiancé Alec.
- **Mrs. Talmage Eglinton**: blonde, childish voice, Cecil; = Ziegler (disguised) = Cora Lestrade. Maid **Rosa** (French).
- **Benzon** (Leopold Benzon): Ziegler's secretary; bold; impersonates "Colonel Anstruther Walcot, 14th Dragoon Guards."
- **Cadaverous clergyman** ("Inspector Chantrey"): burgles John St., Beaumanoir House.
- **Prince**: butler, Beaumanoir House. **Manson**: butler, Prior's Tarrant. **Perrett**: coachman. **Steptoe**: footman. **William**: dreamy footman. **Jennings**: lame third gardener, lassoed.
- **Mr. Bristow** (vicar) and **Mrs. Bristow**.
- **Mayne**: keeper, Sir Claude Asprey's coverts; dog "Tear'em."
- **Pattisons**: family solicitors (Lincoln's Inn). **Morgan's**: bank.
- **Mr. Seaton**: St. Paul purser.

## Events in order

**Ch I (NY, May):** Hanbury leaves dry-goods store (Broadway); searched for stolen goods, sandwiches only. Sees "Three dollars the pair" boot label; jostles Jevons; drink in underground saloon. Jevons shows five $100 notes. Job: plant faked US Treasury Bonds on Bank of England, £3 million. Sail on *St. Paul* for Southampton "day after to-morrow"; call Ziegler at Hotel Cecil. Threat: life worth "five minutes' purchase" if he deserts. Hanbury accepts. Home: top-floor room, German car-driver and Irish porter neighbours. Telegram: "Your uncle and cousin have been killed in a railway accident. Come to England at once. Have cabled a thousand pounds to Morgan's to your credit.--Pattisons." He is now the Duke.

**Ch II (St. Paul):** Duke books as plain Hanbury. Third day: meets Leonie at saloon table ("A penny for your thoughts"). Leonie's mother wants a duke for her. Senator detained at Washington. Girls' plans: Grosvenor Gardens friends, then Paris/Rome, back to America in autumn. Fifth day, near Irish coast: Leonie points out Marker; Duke learns name Marker from steward.

**Ch III (Southampton, Waterloo, Cecil):** Mrs. Sherman invites him to 140 Grosvenor Gardens. Duke gives name Hanbury at Cecil. Ziegler: "Chloroform him"; masked men; Ziegler: "Let him alone, boys. He lied to me." Ziegler reveals agent got Hanbury seated by Leonie; bonds carried by Senator. Ordered back Saturday noon, three days hence.

**Ch IV (Forsyth; the landau):** Forsyth meets Duke on Cecil stairs; visiting Mrs. Talmage Eglinton (absent). Funeral details: late Duke + cousin George killed in racing-special collision en route to Newmarket; buried at Prior's Tarrant. Cousin Sybil Hanbury lives at Piccadilly; Sybil loves Alec. Duke offers Alec secretary post, £800 rising to £2000, dower-house. Duke says he won't live at Beaumanoir House. Landau: Mrs. Talmage Eglinton invites him to tea at Cecil Saturday; Duke refuses; decides to go straight. Plans: Bond Street creditors, then Prior's Tarrant.

**Ch V (Prior's Tarrant):** Sunday; Duke missed Ziegler appointment. Alec's letter: engaged to Sybil; dined with Sadgrove; met Shermans; skipped Mrs. Eglinton's tea. Church; lunch at vicarage. Manson reports Jennings lassoed in copse. Night: Duke's state bedroom; chimney plugged; charcoal brazier in grate; he wakes choking. "Charcoal! Ziegler!"

**Ch VI (140 Grosvenor Gardens):** Tea: Mrs. Sadgrove, Mrs. Sherman, Leonie, Sybil. Mrs. Eglinton visits; General later reveals she ran down a man in Buckingham Palace Road; he saw it. Duke arrives with arm in black silk sling and diachylon plaster; "grazed against wheel getting out of cab." Duke probes Senator's bond mission, warns Leonie; General notes. Duke goes to Alec.

**Ch VII (John Street):** Duke says attempts on life (Jennings, charcoal, carriage). Marker at door: pretends chemist's messenger for "Mr. Crofton"; Duke recognises him. Alec sends Duke to bed in his rooms; Alec goes to club (Constitutional) one hour; password "Rat." Returns 10:30; meets two men on stairs (clergyman, bull-necked man in tweeds/bowler). Door forced with jemmy; Duke gone.

**Ch VIII (Beaumanoir House):** Sybil alone in white drawing-room. "Inspector Chantrey, CID" (clergyman) asks for Duke. Duke arrives, rebukes him. Duke leaves message for Alec: going to seaside. Alec arrives; Duke, Alec, Sybil stay. Sybil hears sawing at Duke's door ~3am; catches tweed man with revolver; Duke disarms him, marches him out. Panel cut with watch-spring saw.

**Ch IX (Strategy):** Morning, Alec reports to General. General plans move to Prior's Tarrant; sends Azimoolah. Steptoe offers apple-woman (Green Park) a coin; she meets tweed/clergy man in Air Street; they leave. Duke refuses police; General proposes house-party; Duke wavers, invites Shermans.

**Ch X (duty call):** General at Scotland Yard: no "Inspector Chantrey." Azimoolah reappears. Shermans accept. General calls on Mrs. Eglinton at Cecil; discovers split suite. Azimoolah as "Thakore of Bhurtnagur" raids Ziegler's rooms; disarms two knife-men. General: "When does the Duke go into the country?" "8.45 from St. Pancras. Alec Forsyth goes down with him."

**Ch XI (terrace):** General at Prior's Tarrant; Azimoolah reports painters with dog-cart ("deer like unto swine"). 8.45 derailed between St. Albans and Harpenden. Alec returns; telegram claimed from "Sybil Hanbury" is forged. Talk: General links Mrs. Eglinton to Ziegler. 2 am terrace: General tackles Azimoolah by mistake; two prowlers flee.

**Ch XII (8.45):** Duke alone in carriage; Kentish Town, Hendon, Mill Hill, Elstree. Tall American magnate boards at Elstree; boot under seat = Marker. Radlett: Marker shows ticket; Duke's trap fails. Obstruction on steep gradient (baulks of timber, ballast); passengers stranded; Marker, tall man, and hatbox man vanish. Duke flees over fence into wood; whistle answers.

**Ch XIII (keeper's cottage):** Duke finds Sir Claude Asprey's keeper's cottage (memory: first pheasant). Keeper Mayne recognises him. Tall American: "Colonel Anstruther Walcot, 14th Dragoon Guards" (card). Duke invents debt to Walcot; escapes via woodshed roof and faggots; £5 note to Mayne. Walks to sign-post; shadowed by Azimoolah; flings himself on him at terrace steps.

**Ch XIV (too many women):** General releases Azimoolah. Duke asks about the Eglinton letter (scented; accepts invitation). General plans. Anonymous note to Mrs. Sadgrove: "There is danger from Ziegler" (same scent). General concludes Eglinton is Ziegler's ally or trying to mislead. Sybil: "Too many women"; she and General confer.

**Ch XV (cure for headache):** Tapestry-room; Leonie sings. Sybil tells Mrs. Eglinton General will confront Ziegler. Mrs. Eglinton "headache"; Rosa. Night: Azimoolah sees her slip out; follows to park wall; dog-cart to St. Albans, "3.15 up night mail." General goes to London next morning; returns: "I have been with Mr. Ziegler this morning." Forged letter to Ziegler (written by General and Alec) sent: Duke submits; secretary to call Monday.

**Ch XVI (delicate mission):** Mrs. Eglinton to London Monday; Alec goes too (leases). Alec tails her to Bond Street modiste. At Cecil: Benzon, "Colonel Walcot" impostor; Ziegler on couch against door; cadaverous clergyman present. Ziegler probes: asks if Duke told Alec or General the cause; Alec denies. Alec receives sealed packet for Duke. Eglinton meets him on stairs, claims jewels; lunch at Kettner's. She asks why he followed; Alec: "I am very far from being indifferent to you, Mrs. Talmage Eglinton."

**Ch XVII (where is the Duke?):** Senator due Liverpool. Duke's room empty; bed slept in; smoking-room window unbolted; Azimoolah tracked him: left ~5–6am, walked to Tring station; 7.30 down to Bletchley junction; to North of England express to Liverpool. Mrs. Eglinton visits library; General says Duke is "gone away for a few hours by an early train on business."

**Ch XVIII (Senator):** *Campania* at Liverpool. Purser Seaton. Duke meets Senator, claims identity; Senator suspicious but accepts. Corridor express, Lime Street; pistol in Duke's pocket; Senator suspects Duke. Mrs. Sherman's letter confirms invitation. Prior's Tarrant. Senator hides bonds in green-and-gold fire-proof safe in muniment room; Duke keeps key.

**Ch XIX (in the crypt):** Late night, General and Senator talk: Cora Lestrade (queen of criminal band; broke jail; Sing Sing). Alec disguised as Duke (make-up), copying limp. Ziegler's letter to Duke (signed "C.Z."): leave crypt door unbolted Tuesday; hand over documents. Alec enters crypt; Ziegler (five men) examines package: tissue paper; appeals to be given back the forged bonds; Alec refuses; lets Ziegler out via garden door. Rosa watching Alec on stairs.

**Ch XX (muniment room):** Duke in dark with revolver guarding safe. Pebbles on window. Ziegler + Rosa enter; Rosa opens window, calls Benzon. Duke turns light on; seizes Ziegler. General, Senator, Forsyth, Sybil arrive. Azimoolah brings in watch-spring man through window. Ziegler unmasked as Mrs. Talmage Eglinton = Cora Lestrade. General explains: Benzon and Lestrade tricked; Lestrade spared Forsyth out of love; Benzon climbs out window. Lestrade allowed to leave next morning; departs early with Rosa, "highest spirits."

**Ch XXI (honor of the house):** Bonds delivered to Bank of England. Duke confesses to General (after hotel visit). Duke confesses to Senator he'd have done the job but for coming on the St. Paul; Senator calls him "a straight man"; Duke asks to speak to Leonie; Senator agrees.

**Epilogue (six months later):** Alec agent of ducal estates; married Sybil in September. Duke and Duchess honeymooning in Egypt. *Standard*: Cora Lestrade (as "Countess Poniatowski") stabbed on Budapest–Vienna train; man in Roman-priest dress arrested. Sybil credits General's insight to woman's knowledge.
